content.text:
Rare as a blanket rule. What I see in your diff is that you've extended the project's Mantine-only convention (`import {\n Table,\n} from '@mantine/core'`) to *every* import in the file, including single-specifier ones like `useEffect` from `'react'` — that's the unusual part, not multi-line imports themselves.

The mainstream default (Prettier, which most TS codebases run unmodified) is: single line up to `printWidth` (80 chars typically), and Prettier only breaks to multi-line — one specifier per line, trailing comma — when the line doesn't fit. Nobody hand-writes that decision; it's automatic and length-driven, so short imports like `import { useEffect } from 'react';` almost never get expanded. Style guides like Airbnb don't add rules on top of this; they just defer to the formatter.

Forcing *every* import onto multiple lines regardless of length, as CLAUDE.md mandates for `@mantine/*` and as you've now done here for all imports, is a deliberate deviation from that default. It buys cleaner diffs (adding/removing a specifier touches one line, not a shared line with unrelated specifiers) at the cost of vertical space and scanability. That's a legitimate tradeoff some teams make, but it's a project-specific choice, not an industry norm — most codebases would flag this as excessive noise from Prettier/ESLint's default config.

If you like the result, worth checking whether your CLAUDE.md convention should explicitly extend beyond `@mantine/*` to all imports, or whether this file should be reverted to match the current documented scope.

It's not just theoretical — there's real overlap. `eslint.config.mjs` currently sets several formatting rules directly: `semi`, `comma-dangle`, `eol-last`, `operator-linebreak`, plus the whole `typescript-eslint` `flat/stylistic-type-checked` rule set. Those are exactly the category of rule Prettier and ESLint fight over if both are left active — Prettier reformats a line one way, ESLint's rule flags it (or "fixes" it back), and you get autofix churn or a red squiggle that never resolves.

The standard, well-established fix is `eslint-config-prettier`: it doesn't add rules, it only turns off every ESLint rule that overlaps with formatting, so ESLint owns code quality and Prettier owns layout. Worth including that in the ticket's scope now, or adding as a follow-up when you actually adopt Prettier — happy to leave SYS-598 as-is and note it as a dependency, whichever you prefer.

content.text: What would be exampkles of the changes made in this codebase if eslint-config-prettier were to be set?

Less dramatic than you might expect — your ESLint config was largely hand-tuned to already match Prettier's defaults, so `eslint-config-prettier` mostly removes redundancy rather than changing visible output. Concretely, in `eslint.config.mjs`:

**Rules it would turn off:**
- `semi: ["error", "always"]` — Prettier also defaults to semicolons, so no diff, just a change of which tool enforces it.
- `comma-dangle: [...always-multiline...]` — Prettier v3's default (`trailingComma: "all"`) produces the same output for anything already wrapped multi-line, so again no visible diff expected.
- `eol-last: ["error", "always"]` — Prettier always adds a trailing newline; redundant.
- `operator-linebreak: ["error", "after"]` — Prettier's own line-breaking algorithm puts binary operators at the end of the line, matching this.
- `react/jsx-wrap-multilines` — Prettier's JSX formatter wraps multi-line JSX in parens the same way this rule does.

**What it wouldn't touch:** everything semantic/code-quality — `import-x/*`, `simple-import-sort/*`, `sonarjs/*`, `promise/*`, `no-console`, `no-restricted-syntax`, the `no-unsafe-*` and other `@typescript-eslint` rules like `prefer-nullish-coalescing` or `consistent-type-assertions`. None of those are layout rules, so `eslint-config-prettier` leaves them alone.

**The more interesting finding:** your config currently has no `indent`, `quotes`, or `max-len` rule at all — I grepped and there's nothing. So indentation and line-wrapping for long expressions aren't enforced by ESLint today; they rely purely on convention and editor tab settings. That means the real effect of adopting Prettier wouldn't be "rules get disabled," it'd be "Prettier starts enforcing consistent indentation/wrapping for the first time" — which is likely to touch far more lines across the repo than the five rules above ever would, including reformatting whichever of those 14 changed files still have inconsistent indentation.
